title: eval-harness: add prompt-regression CI hook + quality gating for eval metrics
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Add a CI hook that runs prompt-set regression checks and surface eval metrics as quality gates. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via repo config.
description: Motivation: Flaky prompt regressions have caused subtle quality regressions in downstream services. This PR introduces a CI hook for the eval-harness that runs configured prompt-set regressions and evaluates a small set of signal metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity/label-accuracy) against a baseline. When thresholds are violated the hook fails the check and reports detailed metric diffs. Scope: - New GH Actions job + reusable workflow - Eval harness runner glue code for CI invocation - Default metric thresholds and a JSON report artifact - Documentation and quickstart checklist - Opt-in repo-level config (eval-ci.yaml) Checklist: - [x] Implement CI job and workflow - [x] Wire eval-harness runner to produce machine-readable report - [x] Add docs and example prompt-sets - [x] Add unit tests for the metric exporter - [x] Add feature flag (repo config) to enable gating Behavior: The CI hook runs after unit tests for PRs against model-serving code, SDKs, and examples. It runs a focused subset of the full eval suite (short prompt-sets designed to be fast <5m) and compares each metric to the baseline stored in the repo under eval/ci-baselines.json. If a metric regresses beyond the configured tolerance the job exits non-zero and posts a comment with the artifact link. Rollout: This is opt-in by adding eval-ci.yaml to the repo. For core redwood repos we will enable the hook for a 2-week pilot for the runtime and SDK teams. Related: ENG-7823, SUP-1124, previous eval-harness CI work (see pr-112345 and pr-107254).

diff_snippets:
--- a/.github/workflows/eval-ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/eval-ci.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+name: Eval CI
+on: [pull_request]
+jobs:
+  run-eval-ci:
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/reusable/eval-ci-runner.yml@main
+    with:
+      prompt-set: 'eval/ci-samples/sample_prompts.json'

+++ b/eval/ci_runner.py
+def run_ci_eval(prompt_set, baseline_path, out_path):
+    report = run_eval(prompt_set, quick=True)
+    metrics = normalize_metrics(report)
+    write_json(out_path, metrics)
+    if is_regression(metrics, baseline_path):
+        raise SystemExit('Eval CI gating failure: metric regression detected')
review_comments: Carlos Mendes (reviewer): The overall approach looks good. Two asks: 1) can we make the default prompt-set even smaller for PRs touching only docs to avoid CI cost? 2) add an escape hatch label to bypass gating for emergency infra fixes.

Ava Li (reviewer): Please add more detail to the report artifact about sample sizes and per-prompt results so engineers can triage. Also add a non-blocking summary comment on PR with the top-3 regressed prompts.
Priya Shah (author): Added per-prompt breakdown and top-k regressions summary to the PR comment step. Updated unit tests to assert presence of per-prompt entries.
Samir Patel (approver): CI run is stable in my local dry-run. Approving — please squash-merge when green.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the CI hook opt-in. Teams will be onboarded and baselines curated over a 2-week pilot. Future work: - auto-update baseline candidate generation tool - dashboards in Redwood Console for CI eval trends - per-team tolerances and override UI
